paragraphs: A student and public reciter of Rabbi; in the Babylonian Talmud he is called Avdan. See his entry.[^1][^2]

notes.text: אמורא here describes the public reciter/interpreter serving Rabbi, not a historical generation. תלמידו refers forward to Rabbi as the teacher. The source itself says full רבי without the added personal name Yehudah HaNasi; the earlier root identification remains archived rather than added to this literal rendering.
The name Avdan and see-his-entry pointer remain Hyman’s statement, without independently binding identities or verifying the destination.
